Hi Maria — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front:

- By default, prompt/completion logs are retained temporarily for operational purposes (debugging, quota metering) and are not used to train models unless the customer has explicitly opted in.
- We provide a tenant-level opt-out ("no-train") that disables flow-to-retraining pipelines; we can enable this per account or via API flag.
- KV cache and prefix caches are ephemeral in the serving layer and are not written to long-term object stores by default. Persisted traces are limited to short-term logs (default 30 days) unless configured otherwise for support cases.

I'll loop in Soojin and Neha for the technical and attestation artifacts — attaching a short policy doc and a SIG packet that includes the technical control mapping. If you want a formal attestation, we can produce a signed PDF (we've done this for other customers).

Next steps: if HealthX needs the opt-out enabled immediately for a staging tenant, tell me the tenant ID and we can flip it and provide a confirmation email.

Best,

Maria — adding a bit more technical detail and references to controls we map in the SIG: 

1) Training and Opt-in
- Our retraining pipelines are decoupled from the serving/ingest path. By default, customer data is not placed into long-term training datasets. Any use of customer data for model improvement requires both (a) account-level opt-in and (b) approvals from our Privacy & Research board.
- Opt-in surfaces: Console toggle (Admin -> Data Controls), API flag (data_collection: "allow_training"), and a contractual clause. We version all opt-in events and store them in an audit ledger accessible to the customer via the Console.

2) Retention windows & ephemeral caches
- Control: Prompt & completion logs stored in short-term datastore (encrypted at rest) with default retention 30 days for the hosted product. 
- Ephemeral serving caches (KV cache, prefix cache) live in GPU host memory and are flushed on VM termination or model swap. They are not checkpointed to object storage unless a customer requests session persistence for product reasons (e.g., long-running chat sessions) — that is an opt-in feature and documented explicitly.

3) Security & evidence
- We attach the SIG response packet with mappings to the SIG questionnaire IDs for the controls you asked about. The packet includes: control mapping, dataflow diagram, and pointer to our SOC 2 report excerpt for logging and access controls.
- For HealthX we can provide a signed attestation that confirms: (i) default no-training behavior, (ii) default 30-day retention for logs, and (iii) availability of the per-tenant opt-out.

Attachments in this thread: redwood_prompt_retention_policy_v1.pdf; sig_response_packet_HealthX.zip

If you want a second-level technical write-up (network diagrams, KMS key IDs, log retention STS policies) we can produce a support packet under NDA.
